title: How to estimate vending machine break-even in RM
excerpt: Build a simple vending break-even model with contribution per sale, monthly site costs and low, base and high sales scenarios.
opening: Start with the money a sale leaves after its direct costs. A product sold for RM4.00 with RM2.20 stock cost and RM0.20 in variable fees contributes RM1.60 towards fixed costs. With RM400 in recurring fixed costs, that illustrative setup needs 250 sales a month to cover those costs. The example uses assumed figures, not a Vendvision price or earnings forecast.
checklist_title: Build a model you can update
checklist: Separate setup costs from monthly costs. Include delivery, installation and initial stock in your cash plan. Treat refundable deposits as cash tied up.
Estimate contribution by product. Deduct stock cost, payment fees and commission charged per sale. Use a mix-weighted estimate if sales vary by item.
List monthly costs. Allow for rent, connectivity, software, regular servicing and restocking travel. Include a budget for waste where relevant, without counting it twice.
Divide fixed costs by contribution per sale. Round up. Use the number of actual trading days to convert the monthly result into a daily target.
Test three demand scenarios. Model a quiet month, a typical month and a busy month. Include holidays or closures where they matter.
Separate operating break-even from payback. To estimate payback, divide upfront investment by recurring monthly cash surplus only when the surplus is positive.
close: After installation, replace assumptions with actual sales, costs and stockouts. A weak result may call for a change in the product mix, servicing route or site terms.
